phase1_leaf_result.part131_scope: 576 finite traces comparing client-carried signed witness, current repository hash-chain, sink incarnation binding, dual current witnesses, a non-rollbackable anchor positive control, and fail-closed refusal across legitimately-old versus common-mode repository+sink rollback histories, reset/rebind, credential freshness, lost prior effects and four transport/retry traces.
phase1_leaf_result.new_narrowing: There are 32 paired no-newer-witness observations in which the currently visible repository/sink state is identical between a legitimately-old g1 world and a world where g2 existed before common-mode rollback. Four strict pairs require opposite decisions for safe useful behavior. Current-only repository/sink/dual witnesses therefore cannot provide both zero-error rollback safety and useful progress. A surviving newer client certificate works only because its durable survival is itself a third non-rollbackable recovery domain; fail-closed refusal is safe but not useful-outcome parity.
minimal_unresolved_children: A zero-cost Chat-native non-rollbackable recovery witness independent of repository+sink common-mode rollback is unproven.
Whether immutable Git object identity plus a separately retained SHA can provide that witness without another durable domain is untested.
Part128 repository-incarnation write-time fencing remains unresolved.

phase1_acceptance.accepted_scope: Prior repository-local effect-state slice only under fixed repository-incarnation assumptions. Part131 adds no generic common-mode rollback acceptance; its 0/96 external-anchor result is conditional on a non-rollbackable third recovery domain, while fail-closed refusal is safety-only.
phase1_acceptance.scope_guard: Part131 is limited to the stated finite common-mode rollback model. It does not prove generic external-sink idempotency, immutable Git retention, arbitrary consensus/Byzantine safety, or Part128 repository-incarnation fencing.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.quota_zero_acceptance_proven: within the bounded role-local finite model and lightweight repository transport only; rate-limit interruption checkpoints to a later invocation without same-run retry
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.richer_mode_protected_manual_execution_d: none for Part131 modeling; a generic independent anti-rollback recovery witness remains unresolved

continuation: Part132: execute one bounded Git-object/retained-SHA recovery-witness leaf. Hold Parts128-131 fixed. Test whether immutable commit/blob identity plus a separately retained SHA can act as the needed zero-cost non-rollbackable freshness witness across branch force-rewind, repository delete/recreate, same-name reuse, unreachable-object retention/garbage-collection uncertainty, response loss, rate-limit interruption and later retry. Separate content-address authenticity, discoverability/reachability, and freshness/anti-rollback. If the SHA itself must survive in another durable domain, count that domain explicitly rather than treating the hash as self-remembering. Use only own clean state and public sources, no hosted compute/coordinator/finite quota/manual execution; absence of a generic guarantee is an unresolved child, not closure.
